record.original_question:
Let f̂ denote the Fourier transform of f. Let H be either L2(R) or the Hardy space H2(R) = { f ∈ L2(R) : f̂(ξ) = 0 for ξ ≤ 0 }. For ψ ∈ L2(R), define ψ_{j,k}(x) := 2^{j/2} ψ(2^j x − k), j,k ∈ Z. Call ψ a Riesz wavelet for H if the wavelet system {ψ_{j,k} : j,k ∈ Z} is a Riesz basis of H.

Is the collection of Riesz wavelets (in this dyadic setting) path connected in the L2(R) norm?

evidence.quote:
Despite several attempts and significant initial progress Problem 2.1 remains open. In
addition, variants of Problem 2.1 for Parseval wavelets and Riesz wavelets are also open.

The other problem solved by Auscher deals with the Hardy space
                          H 2 (R) = {f ∈ L2 (R) : fˆ(ξ) = 0 for ξ ≤ 0}.

We say that ψ is a Riesz wavelet for H = H 2 (R) or L2 (R) if the wavelet system is a Riesz
basis of H. A Riesz basis in a Hilbert space H can be defined as an image of an orthonormal
basis under an invertible operator on H. Every Riesz basis has a dual Riesz basis. However,
the dual of Riesz wavelet system might not be a wavelet system. If it is, then we say that ψ
is a biorthogonal (Riesz) wavelet.

A Fourier transform defined initially for ψ ∈ L1 (R) ∩ L2 (R) is given by
                                   Z

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For f ∈ L¹(ℝ) ∩ L²(ℝ), let the Fourier transform be defined by f̂(ξ) = ∫_ℝ f(x) e^{−2πixξ} dx, and extend it by isometry to L²(ℝ). Let H be either L²(ℝ) or the Hardy space H²(ℝ) := { f ∈ L²(ℝ) : f̂(ξ) = 0 for almost every ξ ≤ 0 }. For ψ ∈ H and j,k ∈ ℤ define the dyadic dilations and translations ψ_{j,k}(x) := 2^{j/2} ψ(2^j x − k). A sequence {e_n} in a separable Hilbert space H is called a Riesz basis of H if it is the image of an orthonormal basis of H under a bounded invertible linear operator on H. Call ψ ∈ H a Riesz wavelet for H if the system { ψ_{j,k} : j,k ∈ ℤ } is a Riesz basis of H. Let R(H) denote the set of all Riesz wavelets for H, regarded as a subset of L²(ℝ) with its norm topology.

Question: Is R(H) path connected in the L²(ℝ) norm, in each of the two cases H = L²(ℝ) and H = H²(ℝ)?
artifact.status_search_result: A survey of open problems in wavelet theory by Bownik states that the path-connectivity problem for orthonormal wavelets, as well as its variants for Parseval wavelets and Riesz wavelets, remain open. Partial results exist (e.g., connectivity has been established for MRA Parseval wavelets and for Parseval wavelets satisfying mild spectral conditions, and convex combinations of orthonormal wavelets are Riesz wavelets except possibly at one parameter), but the full Riesz-wavelet path-connectivity problem in either L²(ℝ) or H²(ℝ) is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Wavelet Theory (Bownik)
status_evidence.snippet: Despite several attempts and significant initial progress Problem 2.1 remains open. In addition, variants of Problem 2.1 for Parseval wavelets and Riesz wavelets are also open.
status_evidence.claim: The path-connectivity problem for Riesz wavelets is explicitly stated as open.
